newsitem.title: FINLAND: LIPPONEN REPEATS EMU DECISION NOT IF, BUT WHEN.
newsitem.headline: LIPPONEN REPEATS EMU DECISION NOT IF, BUT WHEN.

text.p: Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen repeated on Sunday that parliament's vote on EMU next spring will be a decision on whether Finland should join the single currency in the first group, not a choice between in an out.
"The question is, in fact, only about the timetable," Lipponen said in an interview on Finnish radio.
The government's aim is that Finland would join European economic and monetary union from the beginning, scheduled for January 1, 1999, he said.
"In the government we must reach a unanimous decision on EMU ... I am confident that we will do that," he said.
"The government's policy is that Finland would be among the first when and if the third stage of EMU is implemented," he said. Finland was in shape to join EMU, he added.
But it was possible that parliament would vote against Finnish EMU membership, Lipponen said, but did not elaborate. --Helsinki newsroom +358-9-680 50 245, e-mail news@reuters.fi
